response: Malad (ward P/N) billed Rs 7006462 against a monsoon road repair budget of Rs 7700000, using 91.0 percent. Of 141 jobs, 24.8 percent were reopened within 30 days and 59.6 percent met their agreed repair deadline. Malad is a low-lying ward (index 0.6) where flooding is common, and the city had 18 days of heavy or worse rain this season, so some repeat work is expected. Still, Rs 614828 was billed on DLP roads. DLP means the road is still under the original contractor's warranty, so repairs should cost the city nothing. This amount needs review. Also, 7 jobs were priced more than 30 percent above the rate card and should be checked. The top contractor by spend was Western Coast Asphalt Co (synthetic). Example work orders are WO25-00140 and WO25-00552. Ask the ward office whether the DLP road repairs were claimed back from the original contractor.
